name: Town Center (Shaheed Roundabout)
tagline: The everyday heart of Wadi Musa
description: The commercial core around the Shaheed roundabout is where locals shop, eat and catch minibuses. Streets climb steeply in every direction, lined with grocery stores, bakeries, pharmacies, cheap eateries and family-run restaurants, giving a genuine, unpolished slice of daily Jordanian town life away from the tourist strip.
bestFor: Budget travelers wanting local life and cheap food

name: Lower Town (Near the Petra Visitor Center)
tagline: Closest to the gates of Petra
description: At the bottom of the valley, this area clusters around the Petra visitor center and the entrance to the Siq. Hotels, souvenir shops and tourist restaurants line the road, and staying here means the shortest walk to the archaeological site, though it is a long, steep climb back up to the rest of town.
bestFor: Petra-focused visitors who want minimal walking to the gate
pros: Walking distance to the Petra entrance
Easy early starts and Petra by Night
cons: Brutal uphill return to upper town

name: Upper Hillside Hotel Districts
description: The higher slopes above town hold many of Wadi Musa's mid-range and upper hotels, spread along winding roads with sweeping views over the valley and distant mountains. It is quieter and cooler than the center, popular with tour groups, and best navigated by taxi given the distance and gradients down to the site.
bestFor: Travelers wanting comfort, views and calm evenings
cons: Far and steep from the Petra gate
Reliant on taxis to get around

name: Umm Sayhoun
tagline: Bedouin village at Petra's back door
description: A small Bedouin village on the ridge northeast of town, Umm Sayhoun sits near Petra's back entrance and the trail down to the Monastery. Many of the Bdoul families who once lived inside Petra were resettled here, and it offers a rawer, community-rooted stay close to Little Petra and the Beidha road.
vibe: Local, Bedouin, off the tourist track
bestFor: Travelers seeking Bedouin culture and the Monastery back route
pros: Near Petra's back entrance and the Monastery trail
Close to Little Petra and Beidha
cons: Needs a taxi or car for most trips
